intro: Today you learn to talk about **if**: what always happens (If you heat ice, it melts) and what will happen if something happens in the future (If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home). You'll also learn when to say **when** instead of **if**. Warm-up: what happens if you put ice in the sun?
teachingNotes: Zero conditional = if + present simple, present simple, for things that are ALWAYS true: science facts (If you heat ice, it melts), rules of nature and personal habits (If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep). The result happens every time. Watch the -s after he/she/it in BOTH parts (If Budi eats chilli, he gets…). Common error: *'If you heat ice, it will melts' (→ it melts): no will, and never will + -s.

First conditional = if + present simple, will/won't + base form, for ONE situation in the future that may or may not happen (If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home). Indonesian trap 1: 'kalau nanti hujan / kalau besok hujan' marks the future in the if-part, so learners say *'If it will rain, I'll stay home'. In English the if-part already points to the future, so it stays in the present simple (If it rains tomorrow); will goes only in the result part. The same is true after when (When I get home, not *'When I will get home'). Indonesian trap 2: 'Kalau hujan, saya di rumah saja' has no 'akan', so learners leave out will in the result: *'If it rains tomorrow, I stay home'.
Comma rule: when the if-part comes first, put a comma after it (If it rains, I'll stay home). When the result comes first, no comma (I'll stay home if it rains). The meaning is the same.

if vs when: 'if' = maybe (you're not sure it will happen): If I see Budi, I'll tell him. 'when' = sure to happen, only the time is later: When I get home tonight, I'll call you. Indonesian 'kalau' covers both (Nanti kalau sudah sampai, kabari ya = When you arrive, …), so look at whether it's sure, not at the Indonesian word. Common error: *'If I get home tonight, I'll call you' when getting home is certain. For general facts (zero conditional) if and when mean almost the same (If/When you heat ice, it melts), so don't test if vs when on facts.

Keep zero and first apart in exercises: a general fact or habit (no time words, 'every time', 'always') → zero; one situation with a time (tomorrow, tonight, this weekend, now) → first. Many real sentences can take both forms (If it rains, the road floods / will flood); avoid those when testing.

Limits: the learner has NOT learnt the past simple (only was/were) or the present perfect, so keep every example in the present and future. Don't teach the second or third conditional (If I had…, I would…), unless, as soon as, in case, or might/may in the result. Imperatives in the result (If you see Rina, tell her) are fine if the learner uses them, but aren't taught here.

keyPoints.title: Always true: if + present, present
keyPoints.explanation: For things that happen every time (facts and habits), use the present simple in both parts: If you heat ice, it melts. No will. Remember the -s with he/she/it: it melts, he gets.

examples.en: If you heat ice, it melts.
examples.id: Kalau es dipanaskan, es itu meleleh.

examples.en: If you don't water plants, they die.
examples.id: Kalau tanaman tidak disiram, tanaman itu mati.

examples.en: If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep.
examples.id: Kalau saya minum kopi malam-malam, saya tidak bisa tidur.

id.title: Selalu benar: if + present, present
id.explanation: Untuk hal yang terjadi setiap kali (fakta dan kebiasaan), pakai present simple di kedua bagian: If you heat ice, it melts. Tanpa will. Ingat -s untuk he/she/it: it melts, he gets.

keyPoints.title: A possible future: if + present, will + verb
keyPoints.explanation: For one situation in the future that may happen, use if + present simple, then will/won't + verb: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home. Never will in the if-part, even when it talks about the future. When the if-part comes first, add a comma.

examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
examples.id: Kalau besok hujan, saya akan di rumah saja.

examples.en: If you hurry, you'll catch the bus.
examples.id: Kalau kamu cepat, kamu akan dapat busnya.

examples.en: We won't be late if we take an ojek.
examples.id: Kita tidak akan terlambat kalau naik ojek.

id.title: Kemungkinan di masa depan: if + present, will + kata kerja
id.explanation: Untuk satu situasi di masa depan yang mungkin terjadi, pakai if + present simple, lalu will/won't + kata kerja: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home. Jangan pernah pakai will di bagian if, walaupun bagian itu membicarakan masa depan. Kalau bagian if ada di depan, tambahkan koma.

keyPoints.title: if (maybe) or when (sure)?
keyPoints.explanation: Use if when you're not sure it will happen: If I see Budi, I'll tell him. Use when when it's sure to happen, only later: When I get home, I'll call you. Indonesian 'kalau' can mean both, so look at the situation. After when, also no will: When I get home, not 'When I will get home'.

examples.en: If I see Budi, I'll tell him.
examples.id: Kalau saya ketemu Budi, saya akan bilang ke dia.

examples.en: When I get home, I'll call you.
examples.id: Nanti kalau sudah sampai rumah, saya telepon kamu.

examples.en: If it's sunny on Sunday, we'll go to the park.
examples.id: Kalau hari Minggu cerah, kita akan ke taman.

id.title: if (mungkin) atau when (pasti)?
id.explanation: Pakai if kalau kamu belum yakin hal itu akan terjadi: If I see Budi, I'll tell him. Pakai when kalau hal itu pasti terjadi, hanya waktunya nanti: When I get home, I'll call you. Kata 'kalau' dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa berarti keduanya, jadi lihat situasinya. Setelah when juga tidak ada will: When I get home, bukan 'When I will get home'.

guidedPractice.prompt: This is always true. Complete with the verb in brackets: If you don't water a plant, it ___ (die).
guidedPractice.hint: Always true → present simple. It → add -s.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the verb in brackets: If you ___ (be) late for the meeting tomorrow, Pak Hasan will be angry.
guidedPractice.hint: No will in the if-part: if + present simple.

guidedPractice.prompt: Make one sentence. Start with If: it / rain / this weekend → we / stay / at home
expected: if it rains this weekend we'll stay at home
if it rains this weekend we will stay at home
if it rains this weekend we'll stay home
if it rains this weekend we will stay home
guidedPractice.hint: If + it rains (present, with -s), comma, we'll + stay.

guidedPractice.prompt: If or when? You're not sure you'll see Budi today. ___ I see Budi, I'll give him your book.

independentPractice.prompt: Finish the sentence with will or won't: If I have time tonight, I …
expected: if i have time tonight i'll call you
if i have time tonight i will watch a film
if i have time tonight i'll cook dinner
independentPractice.hint: I'll / I will + base form (call, watch, cook …).

independentPractice.prompt: Write a sentence about something that is sure to happen tonight. Start with When: When I get home tonight, …
expected: when i get home tonight i'll cook dinner
when i get home tonight i will take a shower
when i get home tonight i'll call my mum
independentPractice.hint: When + present (I get home), then I'll + verb.

assessment.prompt: This is always true. Complete with one word, the verb in brackets: If you mix blue and yellow, you ___ (get) green.
assessment.rubric: Correct: get (always true → present simple). 'will get' = 50 (good English, but the task asks for one word: a fact uses the present). 'gets' = 40 (no -s with you). 'will gets' or 'getting' = 10.

assessment.prompt: It happens every time. Complete with one word, the verb in brackets: If my cat hears thunder, it ___ (hide) under the bed.
assessment.rubric: Correct: hides (every time → present simple; it → -s). 'hide' = 50 (missing -s). 'will hide' = 50 (the task asks for one word). 'will hides' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the verb in brackets: If the train ___ (be) late tonight, I'll take an ojek.
assessment.rubric: Correct: is (no will in the if-part). 'will be' = 20 (the common mistake). 'are' or 'be' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Complete with will or won't and the verb in brackets: Hurry up! If we don't leave now, we ___ (miss) the bus.
assessment.rubric: Correct: will miss / 'll miss (one situation, now → first conditional). 'are going to miss' = 70 (natural, but the task asks for will). 'won't miss' = 0 (opposite meaning). 'miss' alone = 30. 'will misses' or 'will to miss' = 40.

assessment.prompt: Find the mistake and write the correct sentence: If Budi will come tomorrow, I'll make soto ayam.
acceptableAnswers: if budi comes tomorrow i'll make soto ayam
if budi comes tomorrow i will make soto ayam
i'll make soto ayam if budi comes tomorrow
i will make soto ayam if budi comes tomorrow
assessment.rubric: Correct: If Budi comes tomorrow, I'll make soto ayam (no will in the if-part; Budi → comes). 'If Budi come' = 60 (missing -s). Removing will from the result too ('I make soto ayam') = 50. Leaving 'will come' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with If or When: The film finishes at nine. ___ it finishes, we'll get some food.
acceptableAnswers: when it finishes we'll get some food
when it finishes we will get some food
assessment.rubric: Correct: When (the film is sure to finish). 'If' = 0 (it sounds like you're not sure the film will end).

assessment.prompt: Complete with If or When: I'm not sure Sari is free on Saturday. ___ she's free, we'll go to the beach.
acceptableAnswers: if she's free we'll go to the beach
if she is free we will go to the beach
assessment.rubric: Correct: If (maybe she's free, maybe not). 'When' = 0 (it means you know she will be free).

blocks.text:
A sentence with **if** has two parts:
- the **if-part** (the condition, *syarat*): *If you heat ice*
- the **result** (what happens then, *akibat*): *it melts*

When the result happens **every time**, like a science fact or a habit, use the **present simple** in both parts: **if + present, present**. Teachers call this the **zero conditional** (a *conditional* is just a sentence with *if*).

There's **no will**: ice melts every time, so it isn't a guess about the future. And don't forget the **-s** after *he / she / it*, in both parts: *If Budi **eats** chilli, he **gets** a stomachache.*

id.text:
Kalimat dengan **if** (kalau / jika) punya dua bagian:
- **bagian if** (syaratnya): *If you heat ice*
- **hasilnya** (akibatnya, apa yang terjadi kemudian): *it melts*

Kalau hasilnya terjadi **setiap kali**, seperti fakta ilmiah atau kebiasaan, pakai **present simple** di kedua bagian: **if + present, present**. Guru menyebutnya **zero conditional** (*conditional* = kalimat dengan *if*).

**Tidak ada will**: es selalu meleleh setiap kali, jadi ini bukan tebakan tentang masa depan. Dan jangan lupa **-s** setelah *he / she / it*, di kedua bagian: *If Budi **eats** chilli, he **gets** a stomachache.*

rows.en: If you heat ice, it melts.
rows.id: Kalau es dipanaskan, es itu meleleh.
rows.note: a science fact: it happens every time

rows.en: If you don't water plants, they die.
rows.id: Kalau tanaman tidak disiram, tanaman itu mati.

rows.en: If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep.
rows.id: Kalau saya minum kopi malam-malam, saya tidak bisa tidur.
rows.note: a habit: it's true for me every time

rows.en: If Budi eats chilli, he gets a stomachache.
rows.id: Kalau Budi makan cabai, perutnya sakit.

blocks.text: Not 'it will melts'! Two mistakes in one: a fact doesn't need **will**, and after will there's never an -s. Just say **it melts**.

id.text: Bukan 'it will melts'! Dua kesalahan sekaligus: fakta tidak butuh **will**, dan setelah will tidak pernah ada -s. Cukup bilang **it melts**.

blocks.prompt: If Dimas eats spicy food, he always ___ a stomachache.
blocks.explain: It happens every time (**always**), so use the present simple: **gets**, with -s for *he*. 'will gets' is wrong twice: no will for a habit, and never -s after will.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: If Dimas eats spicy food, he always ___ a stomachache.
id.explain: Ini terjadi setiap kali (**always**), jadi pakai present simple: **gets**, dengan -s untuk *he*. 'will gets' salah dua kali: kebiasaan tidak pakai will, dan tidak pernah ada -s setelah will.

material.title: One possible future: the first conditional

blocks.text:
Now think about **one situation in the future** that **may** happen: *tomorrow, tonight, this weekend*. We don't know if it will happen, but if it does, we know the result. Use **if + present simple, will / won't + verb**. Teachers call this the **first conditional**.

*If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.* (Maybe it rains, maybe not.)

Zero or first? Ask: **every time**, or **one time in the future**?
- Every time (a fact, a habit) → present, present: *If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep.*
- One time, later → present, **will**: *If you drink coffee now, you won't sleep tonight.*

Indonesian trap: *Kalau besok hujan, saya di rumah saja* has no *akan*. English still needs **will** in the result: 'If it rains tomorrow, I stay home' is wrong.

id.text:
Sekarang pikirkan **satu situasi di masa depan** yang **mungkin** terjadi: *besok, nanti malam, akhir pekan ini*. Kita belum tahu apakah itu akan terjadi, tapi kalau terjadi, kita tahu hasilnya. Pakai **if + present simple, will / won't + kata kerja**. Guru menyebutnya **first conditional**.

*If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.* (Mungkin hujan, mungkin tidak.)

Zero atau first? Tanyakan: **setiap kali**, atau **satu kali di masa depan**?
- Setiap kali (fakta, kebiasaan) → present, present: *If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep.*
- Satu kali, nanti → present, **will**: *If you drink coffee now, you won't sleep tonight.*

Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Kalau besok hujan, saya di rumah saja* tidak memakai *akan*. Bahasa Inggris tetap butuh **will** di bagian hasil: 'If it rains tomorrow, I stay home' itu salah.

rows.en: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
rows.id: Kalau besok hujan, saya di rumah saja.

rows.en: If you hurry, you'll catch the bus.
rows.id: Kalau kamu cepat, kamu akan dapat busnya.

rows.en: If Rina is tired tonight, she won't cook.
rows.id: Kalau nanti malam Rina capek, dia tidak akan masak.

rows.en: If the traffic is bad, we'll be late.
rows.id: Kalau macet, kita akan terlambat.

blocks.prompt: Don't drink that coffee now! If you drink it now, you ___ sleep tonight.
blocks.explain: This is **one** night in the future (*tonight*), so the result needs **will**: **won't sleep** (= will not). 'don't sleep' sounds like every night, and 'not will' is the wrong order.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Don't drink that coffee now! If you drink it now, you ___ sleep tonight.
id.explain: Ini **satu** malam di masa depan (*tonight*), jadi hasilnya butuh **will**: **won't sleep** (= will not). 'don't sleep' terdengar seperti setiap malam, dan 'not will' urutannya salah.

id.title: Satu kemungkinan di masa depan: first conditional

blocks.text:
The if-part of a first conditional talks about the future, but it uses the **present simple**: *If it **rains** tomorrow*, not 'If it will rain tomorrow'. **will** goes only in the **result**.

Why? The word **if** already shows we're imagining the future, so English doesn't add another future word there. In Indonesian we often do: *Kalau **nanti** hujan …* or *Kalau besok **akan** hujan …*. English has no word for *nanti* in the if-part. You can add a time word (*tomorrow, tonight*), but the verb stays present.

So check two things in the if-part: **no will**, and the **-s** with *he / she / it*: *If Rina **comes**, …* (not 'If Rina come').

id.text:
Bagian if dalam first conditional membicarakan masa depan, tapi memakai **present simple**: *If it **rains** tomorrow*, bukan 'If it will rain tomorrow'. **will** hanya ada di bagian **hasil**.

Kenapa? Kata **if** sudah menunjukkan bahwa kita sedang membayangkan masa depan, jadi bahasa Inggris tidak menambah kata masa depan lagi di situ. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering menambahkannya: *Kalau **nanti** hujan …* atau *Kalau besok **akan** hujan …*. Di bagian if bahasa Inggris tidak ada kata untuk *nanti*. Kamu boleh menambah kata waktu (*tomorrow, tonight*), tapi kata kerjanya tetap present.

Jadi periksa dua hal di bagian if: **tanpa will**, dan **-s** untuk *he / she / it*: *If Rina **comes**, …* (bukan 'If Rina come').

rows.en: If it rains, I'll stay home.
rows.id: Kalau (nanti) hujan, saya di rumah saja.

rows.en: If Rina comes tonight, we'll eat together.
rows.id: Kalau nanti malam Rina datang, kita makan bersama.

rows.en: If the shop is open, I'll buy some bread.
rows.id: Kalau tokonya buka, saya akan beli roti.
rows.note: not 'If the shop will be open'

id.note: bukan 'If the shop will be open'

rows.en: If you need help, I'll be in my room.
rows.id: Kalau kamu butuh bantuan, saya ada di kamar.

blocks.text: Quick test: find the word **if**. The verb right after it has **no will**. The other part has **will** (first conditional) or no will (a fact that's always true).

id.text: Tes cepat: cari kata **if**. Kata kerja setelahnya **tanpa will**. Bagian yang lain pakai **will** (first conditional) atau tanpa will (fakta yang selalu benar).

blocks.prompt: If Sari ___ tomorrow, I'll show her the new office.
blocks.explain: No will in the if-part, even about tomorrow: **If Sari comes**. And *Sari* = *she*, so add **-s**: 'If Sari come' is missing it.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: If Sari ___ tomorrow, I'll show her the new office.
id.explain: Tidak ada will di bagian if, walaupun tentang besok: **If Sari comes**. Dan *Sari* = *she*, jadi tambahkan **-s**: 'If Sari come' tidak memakai -s.

blocks.text:
You can put the two parts in either order. The meaning is the same:
- **if-part first** → put a **comma** after it: *If it rains, I'll stay home.*
- **result first** → **no comma**: *I'll stay home if it rains.*

When you speak, the comma is a small pause. The same rule works for zero conditionals (*If you heat ice, it melts. / Ice melts if you heat it.*) and for **when** (*When I get home, I'll call you. / I'll call you when I get home.*).

id.text:
Kedua bagian bisa ditukar urutannya. Artinya tetap sama:
- **bagian if di depan** → beri **koma** setelahnya: *If it rains, I'll stay home.*
- **hasilnya di depan** → **tanpa koma**: *I'll stay home if it rains.*

Saat berbicara, koma itu berupa jeda kecil. Aturan yang sama berlaku untuk zero conditional (*If you heat ice, it melts. / Ice melts if you heat it.*) dan untuk **when** (*When I get home, I'll call you. / I'll call you when I get home.*).

rows.en: If you're hungry, I'll make some noodles.
rows.id: Kalau kamu lapar, saya buatkan mi.

rows.en: I'll make some noodles if you're hungry.
rows.id: Saya buatkan mi kalau kamu lapar.

rows.en: If Budi calls, I'll tell you.
rows.id: Kalau Budi menelepon, saya kasih tahu kamu.

rows.en: I'll tell you if Budi calls.
rows.id: Saya kasih tahu kamu kalau Budi menelepon.

options: We'll eat outside if it's sunny.
If it's sunny we'll eat outside.
blocks.explain: The if-part comes first, so it needs a comma after it: **If it's sunny, we'll eat outside.** When the result comes first, there's no comma.

id.explain: Bagian if ada di depan, jadi butuh koma setelahnya: **If it's sunny, we'll eat outside.** Kalau hasilnya di depan, tidak pakai koma.

blocks.text:
Indonesian **kalau** can mean **if** and **when**. *Kalau ketemu Budi, …* (maybe I'll see him) and *Nanti kalau sudah sampai rumah, …* (I'm sure I'll get home) both use *kalau*. English makes you choose:
- **if** = **maybe**. You're not sure it will happen: *If I see Budi, I'll tell him.*
- **when** = **sure**. It will happen, only later: *When I get home tonight, I'll call you.*

So 'If I get home tonight, I'll call you' sounds strange: it sounds like you may not get home! After **when**, the rule is the same as after if: **present simple, no will**: *When I get home*, not 'When I will get home'.

id.text:
Kata **kalau** dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa berarti **if** dan **when**. *Kalau ketemu Budi, …* (mungkin saya ketemu dia) dan *Nanti kalau sudah sampai rumah, …* (saya pasti sampai rumah) sama-sama memakai *kalau*. Bahasa Inggris membuatmu memilih:
- **if** = **mungkin**. Kamu belum yakin itu akan terjadi: *If I see Budi, I'll tell him.*
- **when** = **pasti**. Itu akan terjadi, hanya waktunya nanti: *When I get home tonight, I'll call you.*

Jadi 'If I get home tonight, I'll call you' terdengar aneh: seolah-olah kamu mungkin tidak sampai rumah! Setelah **when**, aturannya sama seperti setelah if: **present simple, tanpa will**: *When I get home*, bukan 'When I will get home'.

rows.en: If I see Budi, I'll tell him.
rows.id: Kalau saya ketemu Budi, saya akan bilang ke dia.

rows.en: When I get home, I'll call you.
rows.id: Nanti kalau sudah sampai rumah, saya telepon kamu.

rows.en: If it's sunny on Sunday, we'll go to the park.
rows.id: Kalau hari Minggu cerah, kita akan ke taman.

rows.en: When the class finishes, I'll eat lunch.
rows.id: Nanti kalau kelasnya selesai, saya makan siang.
rows.note: the class is sure to finish

blocks.text: For facts that are always true, **if** and **when** mean almost the same: *If you heat ice, it melts* = *When you heat ice, it melts*. That's not breaking the rule: a fact happens every time, so it's always 'sure'. The choice matters for **one** situation in the future.

id.text: Untuk fakta yang selalu benar, **if** dan **when** artinya hampir sama: *If you heat ice, it melts* = *When you heat ice, it melts*. Itu tidak melanggar aturan: fakta terjadi setiap kali, jadi selalu 'pasti'. Pilihan if atau when penting untuk **satu** situasi di masa depan.

blocks.prompt: Budi is at work. He finishes at 5 p.m. Budi: '___ I finish work, I'll go to the gym.'
blocks.explain: Budi is sure he'll finish work at 5, so use **When**. 'If' sounds like he may not finish work at all.

id.prompt: Budi sedang di kantor. Dia selesai jam 5 sore. Budi: '___ I finish work, I'll go to the gym.'
id.explain: Budi pasti selesai kerja jam 5, jadi pakai **When**. 'If' terdengar seolah-olah dia mungkin tidak selesai kerja sama sekali.

id.intro: Hari ini kamu belajar tentang **if** (kalau): apa yang selalu terjadi (If you heat ice, it melts) dan apa yang akan terjadi kalau sesuatu terjadi di masa depan (If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home). assessment.zf-3: Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung: If the train ___ (be) late tonight, I'll take an ojek.
assessment.zf-4: Lengkapi dengan will atau won't dan kata kerja dalam kurung: Hurry up! If we don't leave now, we ___ (miss) the bus.
assessment.zf-5: Temukan kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: If Budi will come tomorrow, I'll make soto ayam.
assessment.zf-6: Lengkapi dengan If atau When: The film finishes at nine. ___ it finishes, we'll get some food.
assessment.zf-7: Lengkapi dengan If atau When: I'm not sure Sari is free on Saturday. ___ she's free, we'll go to the beach.
